task.title: SQLite 事务、WAL 与连接隔离边界审查
task.scope: Research synthesis and acceptance-evidence review using a frozen official-source packet. This is not an open-web deep-research pipeline.
task.prompt: 基于提供的 SQLite 官方冻结证据，给出六条结构化结论：外键配置作用域和默认假设，事务中切换外键的行为，WAL 的读写与写写并发，WAL 读快照及升级写，跨连接未提交可见性和例外，BEGIN IMMEDIATE 起始行为与写锁冲突。每条结论填写指定 facts 字段并逐条引用相关 source/excerpt；不做版本性能推断或网络搜索。

sources.title: SQLite Foreign Key Support
sources.hash_scope: SHA256 of exact UTF-8 text field; not a full-page hash
sources.text:
Assuming the library is compiled with foreign key constraints enabled, it must still be enabled by the application at runtime, using the PRAGMA foreign_keys command.
Foreign key constraints are disabled by default (for backwards compatibility), so must be enabled separately for each database connection.
Careful developers will not make any assumptions about whether or not foreign keys are enabled by default but will instead enable or disable them as necessary.
It is not possible to enable or disable foreign key constraints in the middle of a multi-statement transaction (when SQLite is not in autocommit mode). Attempting to do so does not return an error; it simply has no effect.
sqlite> PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.hash_scope: SHA256 of exact UTF-8 text field; not a full-page hash
sources.text:
WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed concurrently.
However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time.

However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time.

sources.title: Isolation In SQLite
sources.hash_scope: SHA256 of exact UTF-8 text field; not a full-page hash
sources.text:
Any write transactions that commit while the read transaction is active are still invisible to the read transaction, because the reader is seeing a snapshot of database file from a prior moment in time.
The attempt by X to escalate its transaction from a read transaction to a write transaction fails with an SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT error because the snapshot of the database being viewed by X is no longer the latest version of the database.
Partial changes by the writer that have not been committed are invisible to the reader.
The combined use of shared cache mode and the read_uncommitted pragma is the only way that one database connection can see uncommitted changes on a different database connection.
In WAL mode, SQLite exhibits "snapshot isolation".
and the two database connections do not have a shared cache, then the reader is only able to see complete committed transactions from the writer.

sources.title: Transaction
sources.hash_scope: SHA256 of exact UTF-8 text field; not a full-page hash
sources.text:
IMMEDIATE causes the database connection to start a new write immediately, without waiting for a write statement.
The BEGIN IMMEDIATE might fail with SQLITE_BUSY if another write transaction is already active on another database connection.

output_contract.claims: Array of {id, facts, citations: [{source_id, url, excerpt_id, quote}]}
output_contract.facts: Exact typed fields from each claim schema; extra prose does not override the structured facts.
output_contract.citations: One citation per required excerpt; URL must equal its source URL and quote must match the complete frozen excerpt after whitespace normalization.
output_contract.limitations: State that the evidence packet covers only the listed transaction boundaries, not performance, deployment safety, all SQLite versions or open-web research quality.

oracle_design.facts: Deep equality against required_facts; exact required claim IDs once each.
oracle_design.citation_integrity: Check known source ID, exact URL, approved excerpt ID, nonempty quote, literal full-excerpt equality after whitespace normalization, and excerpt presence in frozen source.text.
oracle_design.coverage: Every expected evidence excerpt must have a valid citation for that claim. A real but unrelated quote is insufficient.
oracle_design.source_integrity: Recompute SHA256 of source.text UTF-8 bytes before scoring. Retrieval timestamp records collection time, not publication time.
oracle_design.finding: Auditor reviews whether the Orchestrator actually checked all facts and citation coverage, with evidence tied to the result revision. The hidden oracle scores the decision; it is not an Auditor tool.

mutation_candidates.fault: Wrong scope despite an authentic source URL.
Treating a no-op during an active transaction as successful configuration.
Confusing reader/writer overlap with concurrent writers.
Treating an active WAL read transaction as automatically refreshed after another connection commits.
Mistaking immediate acquisition attempt for unconditional acquisition.
Facts may be correct but the acceptance evidence does not cover snapshot/promotion claims.
Nonexistent source ID even when the asserted facts are correct.
